thread:
ashwin: Running a long-running load sweep this morning for the td6-quant model. QPS up to 600. Seeing intermittent p95 spikes that line up with mixed short+long prompt bursts. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:
priya: yep, that rings a bell. CI run yesterday showed a similar hiccup around qps 320-420. thought it was kvcache cold misses but not 1:1 correlated.
jon: can you paste the timeline + any runner logs? curious whether it's precompute/prepare time inflating tail latency.
maria: perf-ci-bot uploaded the job artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/artefacts/1992345610/snapshot.tar.gz
ashwin: ack — uploading the trimmed logs. key snippet below:
```
2026-05-03T09:12:14Z runner: request(id=42) start prepare
2026-05-03T09:12:14Z kvcache: lookup miss for prefix sha256=abc123
2026-05-03T09:12:15Z runner: request(id=42) start generate
2026-05-03T09:12:16Z gpu: token_batch_execute cost_ms=720
2026-05-03T09:12:17Z runner: request(id=42) finish total_ms=3100
```
ashwin: note the prepare->generate gap sometimes >500ms for some short prompts, but GPU exec is fine.
priya: could be batching window jitter: short prompts wait for a batch, then a long prompt arrives and evicts or reshuffles?
taylor: also check the prefill vs decode accounting in the harness. we recently changed instrumentation and might be double-counting socket wait + prepare.
jon: good call. the harness timestamps used to mark 'prepare' included time spent fetching external metadata (tokenizer + config) from the model catalog. when mixed short/long sequences, that metadata call can get serialized.
perf-ci-bot: perf-ci: build 2026-05-03T09:10 triggered. load-profile: mixed-short-long. artifacts: S3://perf/1992345610
maria: also noticed the kvcache prefetch backpressure counter incrementing in those windows. if prefetch is stalled it can push extra latency into the prepare phase.
priya: repro plan: 1) run isolated short-only workload, 2) run long-only, 3) run interleaved short/long with same qps and measure prepare vs generate histograms. I'll spin those up.
ashwin: can we also toggle batching window from 2ms to 8ms as an A/B to see effect? suspect small windows + mixed lengths cause starvation.
taylor: add a metric for 'catalog-lookup-ms' and 'kvcache-prefetch-wait-ms' separately; right now we aggregate both into 'prepare'. that'll let us separate I/O vs scheduling.
jon: i'll open a tiny patch to the harness to split those timers. PR draft: https://git.redwood/eng-ml/runner/merge_requests/487
priya: quick local run results:
```
short-only qps=400 p95=42ms
long-only qps=400 p95=210ms
mixed qps=400 p95=420ms  <-- spike
mixed with batching=8ms p95=160ms
mixed with catalog-cache warm p95=130ms
```
priya: so two things: batching window change helps a lot; catalog cache warm also helps.
maria: interesting that warm cache has bigger effect than batching tweak in your run. suggests catalog lookup hot-path serialization.
ashwin: action items: 1) jon to land the timer-split PR (jon). 2) eng-runtime to add a small in-memory LRU for catalog lookups in the runner (ashwin + taylor). 3) perf team to run a full sweep with multiple seeds and noisy background traffic (priya).
jon: PR posted, added feature-flag to opt-in. patch includes new metrics: runner.catalog_ms and runner.kvcache_wait_ms.
taylor: i'll prototype a tiny in-proc cache behind a feature flag; if memory safe we can enable in Dedicated.
perf-ci-bot: perf-ci: scheduled load sweep matrix: qps=[100,300,500], batch_window=[2,8,16], cache=[cold,warm], run_id=1992345610-01
priya: scheduling note: let's include a 'mixed skewed' distribution where 70% short prompts (<=40 tokens) and 30% long (>512 tokens). that was the worst-case in production.
maria: also include a scenario with forced kvcache miss every Nth request to model eviction storms.
nashwin: thanks all — prioritize the timer split and in-proc catalog cache. Will follow up with a summary tomorrow. :thumbsup:
priya: summary we can paste to postmortems channel once we have CI results.
jon: will add unit tests for the timer changes and a small integration test for the catalog cache flag.
perf-ci-bot: perf-ci: run started 2026-05-03T09:45; expected duration ~45m. logs streaming to S3.
ashwin: ping if anybody sees weird artifact names; I'll collect final graphs and tag in #eng-ml.
